submission.natural_language_explanation: L5/N245+ is a retrospective lexical detector with a sparse, concrete lexicon: it fires on the current token when that token is a scene-setting physical word (landform/weather/terrain and outdoor-activity words such as 'reef', 'ledge', 'cliff', 'cavern', 'cave', 'glacier', 'avalanche', 'powder', 'surf', 'moss', 'beach', 'trail', 'quarry', 'dell') or a bodily/health-experience word ('appetite', 'pills', 'medicine', 'hygiene', 'conscious', 'fasting'), reaching 1-7 on such prompts, while function words, abstract/business/legal prose, everyday basic-level vocabulary ('cat', 'dog', 'house', 'cup', 'door', 'money') and the generic terms of its own domains ('mountain', 'hill', 'island', 'canyon', 'crag', 'water', 'rock', 'grass') stay at or below the activation line; on plain narrative prose the pole still crosses the line weakly (0.1-0.3) in about a third of sentences, and it has scattered single-word hits (e.g. ' directly' in 'follows directly from', ' year', ' while'). It does not look ahead: the determiner one token before a strong noun is flat (0.03) whichever noun follows, activation groups more by the current token than by the next one, and ablating the pole moves the next-token distribution by KL about 1.4e-4.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The storm had been forecast for days, but the station on the ridge had been wrong before, so we packed the van before dawn and drove north along the lake, watching the ice at the edges break into grey plates that slid under the bridge. Jonas had done the route twice, once in summer and once in late autumn, and he talked the whole way about the way snow settles on the northern aspects, how it hardens under the wind and how the slope above the col sheds it in slabs the size of tables. I listened, watched the headlights cut through the sleet, and said little, because nothing I could add would make the drive shorter or the task any easier. We left the road at a turnout marked by a rusted gate and walked for two hours up a logging track that had not seen a truck in a decade. The forest was quiet in the way that cold forests are quiet: every small sound swallowed by the snow, and the only thing moving was the breath coming off our shoulders in slow white clouds. Somewhere above us a bird crossed the gap between two firs and vanished, and the branches where it had sat went on shedding their load long after it had gone. By the time we reached the basin the sun had come up behind the eastern shoulder and turned the whole bowl a pale orange, and the shadows of the pines lay across the slope in long parallel bars. Jonas stopped and pointed. Above the headwall, where the snow had been worked by the wind into a smooth, faintly blue sheet, a crack ran from left to right, and he did not like the look of it. We dug a pit at the base of the slope, cut the face clean with the shovel, and counted the layers with a card: a soft layer, a harder layer, a thin crust that broke under the thumb, and a grainy band beneath it that slid apart when he pressed it. He studied the band, then the slope, then me, and said we would take the ridge instead. The ridge was longer and slower, and it asked us to move together over ground where a fall would mean something, so we shortened the rope and went up in the cold, the wind pulling at the loose end, the snow squeaking under our boots. Two pitches up the ground steepened and the ridge narrowed to a spine of broken blocks; we belayed from a spike of stone and then from the shaft of an axe driven into the crust. It was on the third pitch, just below the summit block, that we found the ledge: a shelf of flat ground a meter wide, sheltered on three sides by a wall of stone, with old cord wrapped around a horn and a rusted piton driven in below it. Someone had bivouacked there long ago and left a tin can and the blackened stones of a fire. We ate out of the wind and watched the clouds move below us through the gap. The summit was a flat plate of snow with a cairn on it and a register in a plastic jar, and we signed it, turned around, and started down.
